text: {"frames":["Anke yanks the bell rope in the cellar, and the bell rings out into the fog over the canal. From behind the wall comes an answer, {c} small knocks like knuckles on wet wood. Old boats from the drowned village are finding their way back by those knocks. Half of the lost boats have already reached the harbour, and the rest are still rocking in the mist. How many boats are still waiting for Anke's bell?","\"Hush, the lamp is listening,\" whispers Edith, the ferrywoman who never speaks above a whisper. The lamp in the mill has been humming all night, and it will not stop. On the shelf sits a jar with {c} sparks of light trapped in it, bobbing like fish. Edith must share the sparks out evenly, half into the lamp and half kept in the jar. How many sparks does Edith pour into the lamp to quiet it?","The cheese in the cellar is humming a tune from far away, and nobody is playing it. The wheels sit in their rows, and {c} of them have a crack in the rind where the sound comes out. The cheese maker tells you that a wheel only sings when it has been turned over, and the sound is halved for every wheel left lying still. Half of the wheels must be turned before the tune finds the way up the stairs. How many wheels must you turn to bring the song up?","Granny Ainsley's needles clicked all night upstairs, and now the scarf is gone from the loft. The last thing she knitted was {c} stitches long, and the loose end ran down through a trapdoor to a floor that is not on the plan. Half of those stitches have been unpicked by somebody in the dark, and the scarf is lying in a heap by the stairs. Half the stitches are still knotted into the wool that leads home. How many stitches are still knitted together?","Ruun smells wet tar and rope before she sees the shelf, where the jars of fog stand in a row. There are {c} jars, and the fog in some of them is breathing, rising and falling against the glass. Ruun knows that the breathing fog is the fog that has lost its way home over the polder. Half of the jars have to be opened to let their fog drift out over the fields. How many jars must Ruun open?"]}
